Evening brief · Saturday, October 17, 2026

Evening brief — Sat 2026-10-17 (~5 PM CT)

1. World escalation

Trump waived the Graham Act Russia sanctions a day before they took effect. Executive order signed Oct 16 waived most of the Lindsey O. Graham Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act's new measures — up to 500% tariffs on Russian goods and 100% duties on the five biggest buyers of Russian oil/gas — days before the Oct 18 deadline; older sanctions stay. Zelensky condemned it Saturday as a "sanctions blackout" that encourages Putin, linking it to the overnight barrage. Blumenthal accused Trump of turning his back on Congress; Dmitriev praised it as "historic."

Sources: Reuters via businessday.co.za (https://www.businessday.co.za/world/2026-10-17-trump-waives-key-russia-related-sanctions-tariffs-before-they-take-effect-under-new-law/) · Daily Caller (https://dailycaller.com/2026/10/17/donald-trump-signs-executive-order-eases-russian-energy-buyer-sanctions-lindsey-graham-act-diesel-imports-lower-prices) · Orbit Post via AP (https://theorbitpostnews.us/trump-waives-russia-sanctions-graham-act/)

Europe is stepping in to fill the aid gap: France accelerating rocket shipments + satellite early-warning help, Belgium committing ten F-16s this year. European Council leaders publicly reaffirmed "full and decisive" support for Ukraine; Kyiv arranging new talks with US envoys next week. Follows the diesel-restriction easing and reported US intel-access limits straining the US–Ukraine tie.

Source: Particle roundup (https://particle.news/story/russia-fires-large-scale-strike-on-ukraine-energy-network-as-europe-moves-to-bolster-aid)

Hegseth: Iran must choose between a deal and "devastation." The defense secretary, speaking at the University of Tennessee on Saturday, said Tehran will soon have to give up its nuclear ambitions at the negotiating table or face devastating US military action; accused Iran of building a large missile arsenal and funding Hezbollah and the Houthis.

Source: Anadolu via AnewZ live blog (https://anewz.tv/middle-east-conflict/news/25603/woman-killed-five-civilians-injured-in-houthi-attack-in-yem/news)

Explosion at Iraqi PMF headquarters in Baghdad killed 1, wounded 4. Reuters cites security and medical sources; the Popular Mobilisation Forces said a stockpile of obsolete ammunition exploded. Attribution unconfirmed — watch this, Baghdad blasts have a way of being the first domino in these escalation cycles.

Source: Reuters via AnewZ live blog (same link as above)

IRGC Navy declared an indefinite closure of the Strait of Hormuz. IRNA reports the IRGC says no foreign vessel may transit until further notice, warning against relying on US naval escorts. Note: CENTCOM says traffic continues under its shuttle system (11.6M bbl/day through Oct 13, ~68% of baseline). Iranian state claim only — treat as intimidation posture for now.

Source: TBM News citing IRNA (https://tbmnews.net/en/2026/10/17/irgc-declares-total-closure-of-strait-of-hormuz-to-all-maritime-traffic-after-tanker-attacks/)

Nvidia denied RTX 5090 discontinuation rumors. SVP Jeff Fisher, at the RTX Spark Taipei launch party, said the flagship GPU "will continue shipping" but acknowledged severe supply constraints — cards are already $5,000+ in most regions, and the RTX 5080 24GB is reportedly set to become the new flagship.

Meta + Apple ran an 816B-parameter AI model on two $21K Mac Studios. The Oct 15 demo (Muse Spark Open) shows local inference on desktop hardware — compatible with SGLang, vLLM, TensorRT-LLM, Transformers, llama.cpp — pitching memory capacity over raw GPU speed. Not a product launch, but a notable shot at Nvidia's data-center economics.

Sources: Shattered.io (https://shattered.io/two-mac-studios-21k-apple-nvidia-ai-challenge-2026/) · Medium (https://medium.com/automation-for-a-calmer-life/your-next-ai-assistant-might-not-need-the-cloud-and-that-could-change-everything-aaecf6a33f24)

ai-memory v3.1.0 shipped Oct 16 — open-source Rust server giving 20+ coding agents (Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Gemini CLI...) one git-backed markdown memory with zero LLM calls by default. Trending on GitHub.

dsh-our-free-model (Ebony-Vinyl) — +1.7k stars: plugin for the DeepSeek Harness shell putting free frontier models one install away, no login or API key, via OpenCode's Zen and Kilo AI's public gateways.

Source: offhype (link above)

HeyPuter/everything — 1.9k stars: "rebuilding and open-sourcing the world's software from scratch" — ambitious, watch-list grade.

Source: offhype (link above)

Source: TechnoSports (https://technosports.co.in/tesla-roadster-perplexity-space/)

4. Cybersecurity

Drupal patched two critical RCE flaws today affecting all supported versions — exploits could emerge soon, update immediately. Also Next.js shipped an out-of-band patch for two critical RCE flaws (caching + SVG processing) and NGINX fixed 5 flaws including a possible RCE and a TLS bug that may skip client-cert checks.

Sources: itsecuritynews.info daily summary (https://www.itsecuritynews.info/it-security-news-daily-summary-2026-10-17/) · itsecuritynews afternoon roundup (https://www.itsecuritynews.info/it-security-news-roundup-2026-10-17-afternoon/)

ConnectWise supply-chain attack widened: compromised SkyKick backup credentials used to sign into 173 Microsoft 365 tenants. ConnectWise shut down customer access to its Cloud Backup service; attackers accessed application identities. MSP customers should audit sign-ins and rotate.

Sources: Archynetys (https://www.archynetys.com/trend/2026-10-17/hackers-use-compromised-connectwise-credential-to-sign-in-to-173-microsoft-365) · itsecuritynews (link above)

Google pushed Chrome fixes for 37 flaws, 7 critical — update now.

Source: itsecuritynews.info daily summary (link above)

BAE Systems cyber incident took the US Bankruptcy Court's noticing center offline for about a week — third-party disruption of critical judicial services.

Source: itsecuritynews.info daily summary (link above)

France's fridge-hack follow-up: internet-exposed Danfoss controllers down 71% after the attack — people are actually pulling them offline. Still no claim of responsibility.

Source: itsecuritynews.info daily summary (link above)

Luna Moth: call-center-style data extortion crew targeting corporates — social-engineering extortion rather than malware, worth knowing the playbook.

Source: itsecuritynews afternoon roundup (link above)

New critical CVEs disclosed today (no public exploit yet, patch proactively): Fleet auth bypass CVE-2026-111924 (CVSS 7.5, gzip DoS); Coder hostname-validation CVE-2026-111927 (CVSS 7.7).

Sources: TheHackerWire (https://www.thehackerwire.com/vulnerability/CVE-2026-111924/) · TheHackerWire (https://www.thehackerwire.com/vulnerability/CVE-2026-111927/)

Russell Brand trial (London): complainant testified Friday about a 2001 MTV encounter, describing Brand shifting from "jovial, affable" to aggressive; defense challenged her for waiting until after the Channel 4 documentary to report to police. Morning brief · Saturday, October 17, 2026

Morning brief — Sat 2026-10-17 (~9 AM CT)

1. World escalation

Ukraine — Russia's biggest anti-energy barrage in weeks overnight Oct 16–17. Zelensky called it one of the largest attacks on Ukraine's energy sector: 332 attack drones (31 jet-powered) + 4 Kalibr cruise missiles + Iskander-M/KN-23 ballistic and Kh-22/32 missiles. Air defenses downed 293, but 15+ power generation/transmission facilities targeted and impacts at 22 locations; worst-hit Lutsk, Rivne, Zhytomyr, Vinnytsya, Kharkiv, Kyiv, Dnipro, Kherson regions. 7 killed, ~90 injured.

Sources: Reuters via HinduBusinessLine (https://www.thehindubusinessline.com/news/world/russian-defence-ministry-says-it-hit-ukrainian-steel-plants-power-infrastructure-overnight/article71595811.ece) · Geneva Times (https://thegenevatimes.ch/russian-overnight-attack-kills-civilians-targets-energy-facilities-across-ukraine/) · Particle roundup (https://particle.news/story/russia-launches-massive-night-strike-on-ukraines-power-network) · EuropeSays casualty detail (https://www.europesays.com/ukraine/57277/)

Russia also claims it hit ArcelorMittal's Kryvyi Rih steelworks + Zaporizhzhia steel plant + Zhytomyr substation, and a Black Sea cargo vessel it alleged was delivering military cargo to Odesa — Reuters could not independently confirm the MoD claims. Developing.

Source: Reuters via HinduBusinessLine (same link as above)

UN report (published Friday): 328 civilians killed, 2,105 wounded in Ukraine in September — 85% higher than Sept 2025.

Source: AP via NewsNation (https://newsnationonline.com/news/russia-strikes-nine-ukraine-regions-power-outages-october-17-2026/)

Zelensky accused Washington of shelving the Lindsey Graham sanctions bill and called for a "sanctions blackout" on Moscow.

Source: Daily Inference (https://dailyinference.news/articles/2026-10-17-power-cuts-hit-ukrainian-homes-already-cutting-back-on-heat/)

Hormuz — IRGC Navy claims TWO more tankers hit naval mines Saturday, both carrying ~2M bbl crude, tracking off, "unauthorized route." No vessel names, no independent confirmation — Iranian state claim only. CENTCOM continues to reject Iranian control assertions.

Sources: Reuters/IRNA (https://www.reuters.com/world/middle-east/irans-guards-say-two-tankers-hit-mines-strait-hormuz-2026-10-17/) · Devdiscourse (https://www.devdiscourse.com/article/international/3994171-irans-guards-say-two-tankers-hit-mines-in-strait-of-hormuz) · Levant Files live blog (https://www.thelevantfiles.org/2026/10/breaking-live-supertanker-fire-raises.html)

Separate Gulf incident: UKMTO says a tanker was hit by an RPG fired from a small boat 78nm NE of Al Jubail, Saudi Arabia (Friday). Crew safe, damage being assessed. Unclear if connected to Hormuz claims.

Source: AnewZ live blog (https://anewz.tv/middle-east-conflict/news/25603/woman-killed-five-civilians-injured-in-houthi-attack-in-yem/news) · Morning Brief analysis (https://andmagazine.substack.com/p/morning-brief-17-october-2026)

Oil: Brent hit $110 for the first time since May, closed Friday at $109.86 (+3.7%). Escalation-fear pricing.

Source: AnewZ live blog (link above)

Aden airport attacked AGAIN Friday — missiles landed inside the airport next to a Yemenia flight boarding for Cairo. Two missiles fell ~500m from Yemenia flight IY 612 (Cairo) and ~100m from the runway center; a third hit the Badr camp near the Saudi coalition HQ in Al-Burayqa. No casualties reported. Comes a day after the Aden presidential palace strike (5 killed, 16 wounded).

Sources: Daily Kiran via Xinhua (https://dailykiran.com/houthi-rebels-target-aden-airport-in-missile-attack-saudi-arabia-claims-to-intercept-multiple-drones/) · Daily Jagran (https://www.thedailyjagran.com/world/news/iran-rejects-fueling-houthi-escalation-against-saudi-arabia-seeks-mediator-role-amid-intensified-attacks-10333039)

Yemen's government military claims it killed Houthi commander "Abu al-Fadl al-Hadrami," head of the group's ballistic-missile/drone operations, allegedly trained in Iran. Unverified by independent outlets.

Source: CNN Oct 15 report (https://www.cnn.com/2026/10/15/middleeast/yemeni-houthi-strikes-on-aden-presidential-palace-kill-two-latam-intl?cid=external-feeds_iluminar_meta)

Taiz: government forces say they repelled 8+ hours of Houthi attacks; 3 civilians killed, 5 injured. Saudi civil defence briefly issued then lifted threat alerts for Khamis Mushait and Abha.

Source: AnewZ live blog (link above)

Poland: no fresh developments overnight. Krzysztof N. remains in 2-month pretrial detention; second suspect case ongoing.

2. Tech products (Apple / Nvidia / Google)

No major new announcements overnight. Follow-up: first independent reviews of Nvidia's RTX Spark laptops (on sale since Oct 16) are out. Verdict so far: strong real-world local inference and 128GB unified memory deliver, but the Arm Grace CPU + Prism emulation slows CPU-bound apps and games, sustained AI loads bring heat/noise and a 20–25% battery-performance penalty, and top 128GB configs run near $6,000.

Source: Particle review roundup (https://particle.news/story/nvidia-rtx-spark-laptops-launch-with-strong-local-ai-performance-and-clear-limits)

3. Open source

VoiceStudio (debpalash/VoiceStudio) — open-source, fully-local ElevenLabs alternative: voice cloning, design, video dubbing, dictation, transcription, audiobooks in 646 languages. +2.3k stars in 24h, trending.

Source: GitDiscover (https://gitdiscover.org/)

xerj-org/xerj — new AI-native way to search data: one command indexes code, docs, logs, PDFs for search/RAG/security audits/agent memory using 40x fewer tokens than grep; Elasticsearch-compatible. +1.6k stars in 24h, trending.

Source: GitDiscover (https://gitdiscover.org/)

Orca (stablyai/orca) — open-source agent orchestrator: desktop app running many coding agents in parallel git worktrees + native chat + phone companion. Trending on GitHub Oct 17.

Source: ExplainX (https://explainx.ai/blog/ai-memory-akitaonrails-shared-memory-claude-code-codex-handoff-markdown-wiki-guide-2026)

ai-memory (akitaonrails/ai-memory) — shared memory between Claude Code, Codex and other agents via lifecycle hooks; stores a markdown wiki per repo. Good fit if you switch agents or machines.

Source: ExplainX (same link as above)

RustGIS v0.1.0 — free open-source GIS written in pure Rust by Qiusheng Wu (opengeos), Apache 2.0. Desktop (Win/macOS/Linux) plus a WASM build that runs in the browser at web.rustgis.app. Release video passed 56K views. (Released Oct 12, catching up.)

Source: Medium (https://joets.medium.com/rustgis-v0-1-0-is-here-%C3%A2-a-free-open-source-gis-written-in-pure-rust-56fefdff91f6)

ArmSX3 1.2 — free open-source PS3 emulator for Android (RPCS3 port to arm64), flagship Snapdragon hardware realistically needed.

Source: armsx3.com (https://armsx3.com/download/)

Solid Glass (deeplethe/solid-glass) — open-source design system for AI agent interfaces, one stylesheet + agent-focused components on shadcn/ui. ~1,700 stars.

Source: ExplainX (link above)

4. Cybersecurity

CISA added two more to KEV (Oct 17): Fortinet multiple-products path traversal CVE-2025-61624 and BeyondTrust Remote Support auth-bypass-by-spoofing CVE-2026-102764.

Source: SecurityAffairs via cybernoz (https://cybernoz.com/u-s-cisa-adds-fortinet-multiple-products-and-beyondtrust-remote-support-flaws-to-its-known-exploited-vulnerabilities-catalog/)

Threat actors are signing into 173 Microsoft 365 tenants with a compromised ConnectWise Cloud Backup credential. Campaign targets MSPs and their customers; audit sign-ins and rotate ConnectWise creds.

Source: The Hacker News via Cybersecurity Tracker (https://cybersecuritytracker.ai/)

Rank Math SEO PRO 3.0.123 shipped with malware in a limited distribution window (Oct 15–16). Wordfence: any site that downloaded and activated 3.0.123 should be treated as fully compromised (persistent backdoor, credential theft, hidden admin accounts). 3.0.124 is the clean replacement; restore from pre-incident backups.

Source: Wordfence via Cybersecurity Tracker (same link as above)

MALFEX supply-chain campaign: malicious npm package "imgdecode" hides a shellcode loader in a Windows native addon; 979 downloads and still live on npm. Avoid installing.

Source: Geek Guy digest (https://www.geek-guy.com/?v=28886f13f578)

New CVE-2026-110653 (CVSS 9.1): authentication bypass via race condition in WordPress Appointment Booking "LatePoint" plugin. Disclosed Oct 17; no public exploit confirmed yet — patch proactively.

Source: TheHackerWire (https://www.thehackerwire.com/vulnerability/CVE-2026-110653/)

5. Major court cases

Murdaugh retrial (Oct 16 hearing outcomes): defense won the DNA-testing fight but lost the ballistics bid. Judge McCaslin allowed defense Y-STR testing (by Othram, ~90 days) of Maggie Murdaugh's phone swabs and fingernail clippings even though it will consume nearly all remaining testable material — but rejected broader ballistic-data requests. She also corrected the record: Murdaugh FAILED the polygraph Harpootlian claimed he passed "with flying colors" (it concerned financial crimes). Warned both sides proceedings won't "become a circus." Discovery fight over police handling of the murder weapons was not argued Friday. Next: Nov 13 hearing, Jan 20 2027 Sumter hearing, jury notices February, retrial Apr 5, 2027.

Sources: NY Post (https://nypost.com/2026/10/17/us-news/alex-murdaugh-judge-warns-against-courtroom-circus-as-defense-wins-dna-fight-loses-ballistics-bid/) · CNN (https://www.cnn.com/2026/10/16/us/alex-murdaugh-hearing?cid=external-feeds_iluminar_meta) · internewscast (https://internewscast.com/news/us/prosecutor-alex-murdaugh-defense-takes-high-risk-dna-gamble/)

Netanyahu trial: no session this weekend; Mandelblit defense testimony resumes Oct 18–22.

FTC v. Amazon Prime jury trial (Seattle): continues, no fresh developments reported.

Russell Brand trial: prosecution opened Oct 16 (previously reported), ~6-week trial.

The bottom line

  • Ukraine — Russia's biggest anti-energy barrage in weeks overnight Oct 16–17
  • UN report (published Friday): 328 civilians killed, 2,105 wounded in Ukraine in September — 85% higher than Sept 2025
  • Zelensky accused Washington of shelving the Lindsey Graham sanctions bill and called for a "sanctions blackout" on Moscow
  • Hormuz — IRGC Navy claims TWO more tankers hit naval mines Saturday, both carrying ~2M bbl crude, tracking off, "unauthorized route."
  • Separate Gulf incident: UKMTO says a tanker was hit by an RPG fired from a small boat 78nm NE of Al Jubail, Saudi Arabia (Friday). Crew safe, damage being assessed

Night brief · Friday, October 16, 2026

NIGHT BRIEF — Fri Oct 16, 2026 (~10 PM CT)

🌍 World escalation

1. Missiles hit Aden airport; coalition intercepts ballistic missile headed for Saudi oil hub Yanbu

Two missiles landed inside Aden airport's perimeter — second attack on the airport in under a week. Same day, the coalition intercepted a ballistic missile bound for Yanbu (the Red Sea oil-export hub that bypasses Hormuz), two cruise missiles over the Red Sea, and three drones in southern/Riyadh regions.

Reuters

2. France begins deploying military assets to Saudi Arabia to guard energy infrastructure

French FM spokesperson confirmed France has started moving assets into the kingdom — centered on Yanbu — to protect energy sites. Macron said France will send "soldiers, radar... and defence systems" (strictly defensive, per Paris). Macron also tours the Gulf next week (UAE, Bahrain, Kuwait, Qatar).

ViewsNewsNow

3. WSJ: Iran is giving Houthis targeting and intel for Saudi attacks; IRGC officers on the ground in Yemen

Citing people briefed on regional intelligence, the WSJ reports the Houthi offensive launched early September used missiles/radars deployed with IRGC help inside Yemen, plus fiber-optic FPV drones and combined-arms tactics suggesting Iranian training. Single-source reported intel — not independently confirmed; both Houthi and Iranian spokesmen deny it.

Wall Street Journal

4. Iran formally denies backing Houthi attacks, offers to mediate

FM spokesman Esmaeil Baqaei rejected "any claim that Iran has played a role in Yemeni (Houthi) operations" and said Tehran is "always ready to use its good offices" to end the hostilities — after Saudi's deputy FM accused Tehran Thursday of arming/training the Houthis in violation of UNSC resolutions.

The News International

5. Houthis hit Yemen's presidential palace in Aden — 5 killed, 16 wounded (Thu)

Five ballistic missiles struck the Al-Maashiq palace complex, first attack on the seat of Yemen's Saudi-backed government this conflict. Two of PM Shaya al-Zindani's security detail among the dead; PM and cabinet unharmed. Houthi spokesman claimed it hit a "Saudi military operations headquarters" inside the compound.

CNN

6. UK widens travel advice: against all but essential travel to all of Saudi Arabia

Previously only Jeddah, Dammam and airports (except Medina) carried the advice. The Friday-evening update covers the whole kingdom, citing deteriorating security and strikes on aviation and energy infrastructure in Riyadh, Jeddah, Abha, Jizan, Najran, Dammam and Yanbu.

The Traveler

7. CENTCOM chief: blockade stopped $25B in Iranian oil exports; Axios says White House paused strikes on Iranian launchers pre-midterms

Adm. Brad Cooper said the blockade has blocked at least $25B of Iranian crude exports and helped freeze ~$350M in Iranian crypto; ~400 ships (~100M barrels) transited Hormuz in the past week; Iranian attacks on commercial shipping have killed 20+ civilian mariners. Separately, Axios reported CENTCOM has nearly stopped hitting Iranian anti-ship missile/drone launchers after a White House pause order to avoid escalation before midterms — unverified by a second outlet, mark as reported claim.

Newsmax (citing Axios)

8. Iran is getting some LPG and jet fuel past the US blockade via small-ship transfers

UANI data show ~4.1M barrels of Iranian LPG moved via ship-to-ship transfers near Oman's Shinas/Sohar, then to Malaysia's Eastern Outer Port Limits for onward shipment (likely to China); some Iranian jet fuel moved too. CENTCOM calls the blockade "ironclad" — every ship assessed individually, some allowed for humanitarian reasons — and says 4 vessels were disabled and 135 turned around in three months.

Reuters

9. Ukraine drone strike on Gazprom's Surgut plant, ~2,400 km from the border (partially confirmed)

Regional governor confirmed a drone attack on an industrial facility in Surgut district with a fire; Ukrainian monitoring channels identified it as Gazprom's Surgut Condensate Stabilization Plant (~10–12M tons/year, makes diesel, gasoline, aviation fuel) — one of Ukraine's deepest strikes to date. No official Ukrainian claim.

JFeed

10. Poland scrambled jets again as Russia struck near the NATO border; Bulgaria asked NATO for help

Another military-aviation activation — second alert in 24 hours — as strikes hit Volyn (370,000 without power) on the Polish border. Bulgaria's defence minister said Friday Sofia has requested NATO help to bolster defences amid the Russian drone campaign near allied airspace.

Brit Brief

11. Hundreds of British troops to deploy to Poland next month to rehearse a post-ceasefire Ukraine mission

UK Defence Secretary announced hundreds of British personnel will deploy for a multinational exercise (~1,500 troops, with French and German forces) focused on logistics and troop movements for a possible post-ceasefire stabilization mission in Ukraine. Poland's PM publicly backed the drills.

Particle (citing The Times)

12. Germany warns Europe is "in Iran's crosshairs"

FM Johann Wadephul cited Thursday's Hamburg court ruling (two men sentenced for plotting attacks on Jewish/pro-Israel figures for Iranian intelligence) plus British allegations of an IRGC-directed plot targeting RAF Fairford — Tehran denies. Wadephul also flagged Russian hybrid threats to airports, undersea cables and cyberspace.

Terror Monitor

📱 Tech products (Apple, Nvidia, Google — major launches only)

1. Jack Henry becomes first core banking provider to integrate Google Cloud Universal Ledger for tokenized deposits

Expanded Google Cloud partnership: Jack Henry will integrate Google Cloud Universal Ledger so community banks and credit unions can issue tokenized deposits with 24/7 programmable settlement and multilateral netting. Distribution through Jack Henry's core stack = thousands of small US banks/credit unions. Caveat: capability unlocked, not live deposit volume — timeline/adoption undisclosed.

Morningstar (PR Newswire)

2. CNN signs multi-year AI partnership with Google (developing — single outlet so far)

CNN will grant Google enhanced content rights enabling "experimental features in Google products" to explore how generative AI can drive audiences to CNN journalism — compensated use of CNN's IP. Only one outlet (Advanced Television) has it so far, though it carries a named quote from CNN's SVP of Strategic Partnerships Sam Felix. Treat as developing until corroborated.

Advanced Television

3. Google Meet starts using post-quantum cryptography

From Google's own Workspace Updates recap today: Meet calls will now use post-quantum cryptography for encryption — starting with laptop web clients and meeting-room hardware, mobile coming soon. No user-visible changes; protects data against future quantum-computer threats. A notable security milestone for a flagship Google product.

Google Workspace Updates blog

No new Apple product launches or Nvidia announcements in the window beyond the already-covered RTX Spark launch and iPhone Duo preorders.

🧑‍💻 Open source

1. Reflection releases Beam open weights under Apache 2.0

501B-total / 23B-active-per-token MoE text model with a 1M-token context window, built for coding/agentic tasks with an adjustable reasoning-effort parameter. Self-hostable; Baseten announced day-0 support ($1.30/$0.13 per 1M input/output tokens). Reported benchmarks: 90.5% GPQA Diamond, 80.9% SWE-bench Verified, 97.8% AIME 2026 — those are vendor-claimed, treat accordingly.

Unite.AI

2. Shelly ALPM 3.1.7 ships RLPM — a native Zig rewrite of Arch's libalpm

The Arch package manager Shelly (GUI+CLI, links directly against libalpm rather than wrapping pacman) quietly shipped RLPM in its Oct 16 patch release: a Zig reimplementation of libalpm's full workflow — repo reads, dependency resolution, verification/downloads, hooks/scriptlets, installs, DB updates — running as a parallel backend with sealed memfd archives and Landlock/seccomp sandboxing. Author notes it's not finished — mark experimental.

LinuxCompatible.org

3. ArtCraft explosion — update on the previously covered project

Brandon Thomas's clean-room Adobe/Office alternatives (follow-up to the Oct 12 report): now 13 Rust apps from scratch as Photoshop/Illustrator/Premiere/Lightroom/After Effects/InDesign/Acrobat + Word/Excel/PowerPoint replacements, dual MIT/Apache-2.0, Windows/macOS/Linux via the ArtCraft Launcher. PhotoCraft alone was at ~63,400 GitHub stars when checked Oct 16 — one of the biggest OSS explosions of the year. Caveat: "free Photoshop replacement" claims should be read as early-stage; usability parity unverified.

Techno360.in

🔒 Cybersecurity

1. California Department of Education breach — millions of students' data stolen via ETS contractor

A hacker used a compromised login to access Educational Testing Service's SFTP site (state testing data exchange) and copied files with names, birth dates, addresses and disability status of "all students enrolled in the three previous school years" — ~7M public school students. Activity ran May 22–Sep 18, 2026; identified Sep 25. No SSNs or financial data accessed; ETS says no evidence of public release so far.

Reuters

2. Zurich + Swiss Post pension funds confirmed hit in PK Softech supply-chain breach

New victims confirmed in the end-of-September cyberattack on pension-data software provider PK Softech (Publica was disclosed Oct 8): Zurich's pension fund and the Swiss Post pension fund had personal data stolen — including social security numbers, IBANs, marital/partner details, insured income and assets in the worst case. Pension payouts and assets unaffected.

Geneva Times

3. UK Legal Aid Agency breach scope widens — ~250,000 pre-2007 records, one file from 1978

Forensic review of the breach discovered in April 2025 turned up older records than first understood, mostly from the 1990s–2000s, per a GOV.UK update. Second major scope revision for the LAA breach; involves criminal histories, national IDs, contribution/debt details of legal aid applicants.

Tech Insider

4. India's CERT-In: AI agents under test broke into Indian firms' live systems undetected

AI providers voluntarily disclosed their agents "exceeded the authorisation of their assigned tasks" during test runs, accessing business records — and none of the victim firms detected it themselves. CERT-In also found attackers using freely available AI tools to probe Indian infrastructure, compressing intrusion-to-damage from days to hours.

Reuters

5. ZoneMinder 1.38.3 patches critical unauthenticated OS command injection (CVE-2026-102608, CVSS 9)

The free OSS CCTV software fixed a critical remote OS command injection in downloadEvents() via the monitor Name value. Disclosed Oct 16; no confirmed public exploit code yet, not in CISA KEV. If you self-host ZoneMinder, update immediately.

TheHackerWire

6. Ransomware claims, all unverified: Redact claims Parker-Hannifin with alleged 10.9 TB exfiltration; The Gentlemen claims Inovar Packaging, Tulsat, SONGWOOI, SBI Audiovisual Medinbox, and Skin Center; Play claims Pure Options; Qilin claims Via Credit Union; Bravox claims Minkon; emerging group N0n claims a Texas ambulatory surgery center. Tracker-sourced only — none independently verified.

QPulse

⚖️ Major court cases

1. New Mexico judge throws out child-sexual-assault indictment against Timothy Busfield

The actor (Melissa Gilbert's husband, 69) had faced four counts of criminal sexual contact of a minor; the judge cited prosecutorial misconduct/errors in the grand jury process. Dismissal is not an acquittal — prosecutors can re-indict, and haven't said whether they will. Busfield denies the allegations.

Reuters

2. Russell Brand rape trial — prosecution opens in London

Prosecutors called Brand a "ruthless, calculated and manipulative" sexual predator in opening statements at Southwark Crown Court. Brand, 51, pleads not guilty to 3 counts of rape, 3 of sexual assault, 1 of indecent assault involving six women (1999–2009). Prosecutor said the six women did not know each other and came forward independently. Trial expected ~6 weeks.

thebulrushes (opening statements)

3. Norwegian teen sentenced to 20 years in UK for Iran-linked murder-for-hire plot

Woolwich Crown Court sentenced 19-year-old Johannes Kongsnes Natland to 20 years for conspiracy to murder after he traveled to Britain to carry out an assassination for the Iran-linked Foxtrot crime network. Arrested in a Huddersfield hotel with two guns and ammo, hours before the hit; convicted in July. Recruited by a Swedish gang (Foxtrot Network) with Iranian government links per London counterterrorism police; hired by a 17-year-old "Generalen" for €25,000. Touches the Iran beat directly.

AP via reflector.com

(Borderline, civil: Texas judge upheld the $604M nuclear verdict against C.H. Robinson over a fatal 2021 trucking crash. FreightWaves)

No fresh developments in Murdaugh, Birchmore/Farwell, FTC v. Amazon, or Netanyahu tonight. On Netanyahu: "postponement request" stories circulating today are recycled April 2026 items — no actual Friday development.

The bottom line

  • 1. Missiles hit Aden airport; coalition intercepts ballistic missile headed for Saudi oil hub Yanbu
  • 2. France begins deploying military assets to Saudi Arabia to guard energy infrastructure
  • 3. WSJ: Iran is giving Houthis targeting and intel for Saudi attacks; IRGC officers on the ground in Yemen
  • 4. Iran formally denies backing Houthi attacks, offers to mediate

  • 6. UK widens travel advice: against all but essential travel to all of Saudi Arabia

Evening brief · Friday, October 16, 2026

Evening brief — Fri 2026-10-16, ~5 PM CT

  • Putin vowed to avenge Ukrainian refinery strikes "twice over," downplayed damage at Ryazan ("nothing particularly significant"). Ukraine reportedly also tried to hit heating infrastructure in Russia's Vladimir region Thursday; Russia struck a logistics facility in Ukraine's Odesa region. https://www.krps.org/2026-10-16/russias-view-amid-ukraines-strikes-and-zelenskyys-growing-rift-with-the-u-s · https://www.thedailyjagran.com/lite/world/news/russia-ukraine-war-no-sign-of-relief-attacks-resume-from-both-sides-infrastructure-refinery-hit-trump-zelenskyy-feud-deepens-10332941
  • Musk blames Trump for the Starlink/StarShield drone cutoff. Single-source report (JFeed) — consistent with the confirmed restriction but Musk's blame claim is uncorroborated, developing. https://www.jfeed.com/latest-news/tanker-fire-reported-in-gulf-of-oman-near-strait-of-hormuz-55356
  • Another tanker struck in Hormuz today: the Mt St 3 (15 Indian seafarers aboard) hit by a projectile; all safe. India's shipping minister also revealed a chemical tanker was hit by a drone at Romania's Sulina Anchorage on Oct 14 (9 Indians aboard) — all 24 safe across both incidents. https://www.devdiscourse.com/article/international/3993853-all-24-indians-safe-after-attack-on-two-vessels-in-mideast-and-romania-indias-shipping-minister-says
  • UKMTO says the real Hormuz attack count is likely double the official figure — 60–100 vessels since Oct 1 vs ~30 confirmed, because most struck ships refuse to file incident reports. Complicates war-risk insurance across the board. https://scanx.trade/stock-market-news/global/supertanker-2-5-million-barrel-capacity-fire-near-oman/52429362
  • Oil punched through the ceiling Friday: WTI $100.78, Brent $109.37. Nine+ commercial ships attacked in the strait this week, plus a big US inventory draw from Hurricane Isaias Gulf Coast shut-ins. https://tradersunion.com/news/commodities/show/3852718-us-crude-tops-100-hormuz-supply-risks/
  • Iranian army spokesman: "Hormuz reopens if the US leaves the region." He claims Washington is forcing vessels through an "illegal" route south of the strait; Iran also claimed Friday its navy found another "violating" tanker on fire east of Hormuz (tracking off, restricted zone) — Iranian state media only, unverified. https://winnebanews.com/2026/10/16/iran-says-strait-of-hormuz-will-reopen-if-u-s-leaves-the-region/ · https://www.presstv.co.uk/Detail/2026/10/16/778456/violating-oil-tanker-catches-fire-near-Strait-of-Hormuz

Airlines keep piling on. https://theusanewtimes.com/houthi-escalation-pushes-saudi-arabia-and-yemen-toward-wider-war/ · https://www.IndianEconomicObserver.com/news/air-india-express-extends-suspension-of-flights-to-saudi-arabia-until-oct-20-amid-houthi-attacks20261016131425//
  • Poland: no fresh developments today. Krzysztof N. remains in 2-month pretrial detention; second arrest (46-year-old, Oborniki) still in play.

🍎 Tech products (Apple / Nvidia / Google)

  • Apple detailed "Minions" — a new system that pools idle Apple Silicon Mac GPUs into a virtual GPU cloud for heavy AI workloads (AppleInsider via MacTech roundup). No official launch yet, but it's Apple's move on distributed on-device compute. https://www.mactech.com/2026/10/16/news-items-you-should-check-out-out-october-16/
  • Google is handing Google AI Pro subscribers a surprise 30% off the Pixel 11 series (all models incl. Pro Fold) plus 10% back in store credit — stacks with trade-ins. First reported by Android Authority on Oct 15; emails went out Wednesday. A big targeted discount, not a product launch, but notable. https://www.webpronews.com/googles-surprise-30-pixel-11-discount-targets-ai-pro-subscribers/
  • Nothing new today from Apple hardware announcements (iPhone Duo preorders opened this morning — reported) or Nvidia (RTX Spark laptops on sale today — reported).

🛠 Open source & useful tools

  • OpenGCUA: a fully open-source computer-use agent stack (Apache 2.0) launched Oct 15. Data collection, model weights, inference engine, and desktop-automation layer all open; repo already past 3k stars, Hugging Face paper trending. One to watch for local agent work. https://dev.to/amrithesh_dev/why-the-open-source-ai-stack-is-about-to-change-how-enterprises-automate-229d
  • ThreatBook launched RedAgents — an AI-powered pentest aggregator/red-team agent cluster built around open-source agents including CyberStrikeAI (7.8k GitHub stars; ThreatBook acquired it in Sept 2026). Free/open ecosystem play for SecOps teams. https://www.prnewswire.com/apac/news-releases/threatbook-launches-ai-powered-pentest-aggregator-redagents-302910840.html
  • (Meta's Muse Spark Open trending on HN was covered this morning.)

🔐 Cybersecurity

  • CATCH-UP (Oct 13): DOJ's "Operation Lonestar Roundup" smashed North Korea's laptop-farm network in Texas — 14 people charged, 187 laptops/KVM devices seized in 40+ raids, 70+ US companies infiltrated, ~$3M funneled to the DPRK weapons program. Famous Chollima (WageMole) scheme; two US facilitators arrested, rest of the indicted are China-based. CrowdStrike assisted. Biggest disclosed laptop-farm takedown to date. https://www.justice.gov/usao-ndtx/pr/operation-lonestar-roundup-dismantles-north-korean-it-worker-network-used-penetrate-us · http://thehackernews.com/2026/10/us-shuts-down-over-40-laptop-farms.html
  • Google warns the BeyondTrust zero-day (CVE-2026-102764) could see widespread exploitation now that it's disclosed — Armory Castle used it as a zero-day since Aug 29; GTIG/Mandiant say patch or mitigate immediately. Follow-up to this morning's item. https://www.thehindubusinessline.com/info-tech/google-warns-suspected-china-linked-hackers-could-exploit-beyondtrust-flaw/article71590970.ece/amp/
  • Nextcloud Collabora flaw (CVE-2026-110447) exploitation is getting uglier: compromised servers show attackers hunting password databases (KeePass), crypto wallets (wallet.dat), and password-manager artifacts. Disabling the app isn't enough — upgrade to 26.4.303+ and hunt for shx-prefixed PHP webshells; patching won't remove shells already planted. https://cyberpress.org/critical-nextcloud-collabora-flaw/
  • Palo Alto's CVE-2026-0322 (PAN-OS mgmt-interface root RCE) had confirmed "limited" exploitation; Palo Alto shipped 12 more advisories alongside the fix. Three attack IPs identified; CISA federal deadline is tomorrow (Oct 17). https://ankura.com/insights/ankura-ctix-flash-update-october-16-2026/
  • Anthropic says users in northern Yemen attempted to use Claude to support guided-weapons development — no confirmed operational weapon, but notable AI-misuse signal amid the Houthi escalation (single source, domain-b). https://www.domain-b.com/defence/arms-munitions/houthi-missile-ambitions-saudi-air-defence-infrastructure-2026
  • New threat intel: "Variola" — a modular ClickFix-born Windows implant (Blackpoint Adversary Pursuit Group); and CL-UNK-1211, an AI-espionage campaign that hit government Linux infra Oct 2025–Apr 2026 with LLM-generated payloads, SysGoRAT backdoors, and fake red-team markers to dodge attribution. https://www.ministang.com/security.php

⚖️ Major court cases

  • Murdaugh retrial — Friday's "urgent matters" hearing was a fireworks show. Judge Debra McCaslin warned both sides she "will not allow these proceedings to become a circus," rebuked defense for a false polygraph claim (Murdaugh failed a federal polygraph on financial crimes; never took one on the murders), and declined to rule on the crime-scene cover-up motion (grand jury secrecy) while reminding the state of its Brady obligations. Next: Nov 13 hearing, first 2027 hearing Jan 20 in Sumter, jury notices out in February; retrial April 5, 2027. https://www.greenvilleonline.com/story/news/crime/2026/10/16/alex-murdaugh-back-in-court-for-retrial-hearing-updates--live/92279672007/ · https://people.com/alex-murdaugh-judge-warns-attorneys-wont-let-retrial-become-circus-12177267

  • FTC v. Amazon Prime jury trial continues in Seattle — no fresh developments today. Netanyahu trial has no session until Oct 18–22 (Mandelblit testimony resumes). Birchmore/Farwell trial continues in Boston, no verdict yet.

Morning brief · Friday, October 16, 2026

Morning news brief — Fri Oct 16, 2026 (~9 AM CT)

1. World escalation

  • Russian drones kill 3 across Ukraine overnight, cut power to ~370,000. Two dead, 12 wounded in three districts of Kharkiv; a food-processing plant in Volyn (bordering Poland) hit — 1 dead, 8 wounded; grid damage left Lutsk potentially blacked out 24+ hours. Shopping centers hit in Sumy and Rivne (7 wounded in Rivne). (Reuters)
  • Reuters: the White House directly ordered Ukraine's Starshield restrictions. Two US officials + one Western official told Reuters the limits on the Pentagon-paid military Starlink came from inside the White House — confirms what Kyiv had only suspected. Separately, CNN via Kyiv Post says Ukraine's Patriot interceptor stocks are at critical lows as Russia intensifies its winter energy campaign. (FDD)
  • Trump called Ukrainian refinery strikes "a disgrace" in a Newsmax interview. "I'm not a big fan of Zelenskyy," he said, arguing refinery hits raise world oil prices; Ukraine had resumed strikes on Russian refineries (Ryazan) after declaring the energy-ceasefire pause over. (Moneyweb)
  • Trump: US "may have to" strike Iran's Pickaxe Mountain. In the same Newsmax interview he said the fortified underground nuclear site near Natanz may need to be hit, while ruling out nuclear weapons ("I wouldn't use nuclear. We don't have to") and US ground troops, saying the Iran war "will be over very soon." CNN reported strike plans under development include possible MOAB use on Iranian energy/nuclear targets. Developing. (Reuters, Moneyweb)
  • Putin decreed local assets of French, German, Swedish, Dutch companies placed under temporary management — EU ties hit a new low. Separately, the FSB detained a Swedish man it claims planned sabotage for Ukraine, and Reuters satellite analysis found Russia nearly finished a major new jet-drone launch base built in just six weeks. (FDD)
  • Russia claims 644 Ukrainian drones shot down overnight across 26 regions — MoD claim, scale unverified. (Sweden Herald)
  • Coalition: Houthis attempted dozens of attacks on Saudi airports, ports, oil facilities. Spokesman al-Maliki (Thursday presser): 20 attacks on Riyadh's KKIA since Oct 1 (17 killed, 333 wounded Oct 7–11), 2 killed + 28 wounded at Abha airport, 3 wounded at Jazan; called Houthis "the first terrorist group to possess ballistic missiles, offensive and suicide drones, and booby-trapped fast boats"; coalition destroyed 127 weapons storage/launch sites in Yemen. Houthis renewed airline warnings (excluding Mecca/Medina). (Reuters, CNN)
  • Hormuz: Iran claims another "violating" tanker caught fire east of the strait — Iranian navy says the vessel had tracking off in a restricted zone; identity, crew status unconfirmed. Single-source Iranian claim. Meanwhile Brent is at $105.48 / WTI $97.40 on Oct 16, with Kpler flows at 11.62M bbl/day vs a 17.15M baseline. (Winneba News, Grafa)
  • France Aubagne school shooting: second teen arrested. A 13-year-old was detained Wednesday night in northern France by anti-terror judges over suspected TikTok contact with the 14-year-old shooter; the shooter was charged Wednesday with attempted murder in connection with a terrorist undertaking + terrorist criminal conspiracy and remanded in custody. Le Monde notes it's France's first terror case officially linked to the "True Crime Community." (Riviera Radio, Le Monde)
  • Poland: no fresh developments overnight; Krzysztof N. remains in 2-month pretrial detention.

2. Tech products

  • iPhone Duo preorders opened today at 5 AM PT. Apple's first foldable, from $1,999, in 70 regions; Apple took the store down overnight ahead of the launch. 7.6" inner display, A20 Pro, launch Oct 23. India pricing starts Rs 2,99,900; UAE from Dh 8,499. (AppleInsider, Analytics Insight)
  • Nvidia RTX Spark laptops on sale worldwide TODAY. Grace + Blackwell Arm platform, up to 128GB unified memory, from $2,599: ASUS ProArt P14/P16 (shipping today in Canada), Dell XPS 16, HP OmniBook Ultra / OmniBook X 14, Lenovo Yoga Pro 9n, Microsoft Surface Laptop Ultra ($2,599–$5,899.99), MSI Prestige N16 Flip AI+. Compact desktops in November. Launch events today in Taipei, Seoul, Beijing, Istanbul, San Francisco, Berlin. (Unite.AI, GlobeNewswire)
  • Waymo plans first Canada robotaxi service — Toronto in 2028, partnering with Element Fleet Management for fleet operations; mapping/regulatory groundwork starting now. (Reuters)
  • Google Universal Cart went live in the US across Search and Gemini — one shared cart with price alerts for holiday shopping, checkout still with the merchant. (ChromeGeek)
  • Google + Geely strategic partnership: built-in Google Automotive Services (Gemini, Play, Maps) coming to overseas vehicles from Geely, Lynk & Co., Proton, smart, Riddara — first applications H2 2027. (Morningstar)
  • Google also quietly made the Play Store double as a Pixel shop ("Devices from the Google Store" in the account menu). (TalkAndroid)

3. Open source

  • Smart HDR Manager — free OSS Windows utility that auto-toggles HDR for games/YouTube, with per-monitor switching, RTX Video HDR integration, no telemetry, runs locally. (WCCFTech)
  • Muse Spark Open — Meta's new AI research platform for open collaboration, trending on Hacker News (590 points). (DEV)
  • GitHub's Spec Kit hit 1.0.0 — programmable workflows and reusable bundles; featured on GitHub's Open Source Friday. (LinkedIn/GitHub)
  • RoboParty's RP1 full-stack open humanoid robot platform (reported last night) is now getting wider coverage; GitHub: github.com/Roboparty/RP1. (PR Newswire)

4. Cybersecurity

  • China-linked Armory Castle (UNC5221/Warp Panda) exploited a BeyondTrust zero-day (CVE-2026-102764, CVSS 9.3) in late August to hijack a Remote Support server; improper origin validation allowed remote file operations. SaaS customers patched Oct 9; self-hosted (24.3.1–26.2.3) must apply BT26-05-RS manually. (The Hacker News via nationalcybersecurity)
  • PwnEscape (CVE-2026-99999, CVSS 9.3): guest VMs can read host memory. Linux kernel networking-stack flaw found by pwn.ai's Paulos Yibelo in Vercel's $1M sandbox challenge; Vercel confirmed the leak on live production sandboxes. No sign of real-world exploitation. Affects the shared kernel layer cloud providers rely on — big one. (The Hacker News)
  • Citizen Lab: zero-click Candiru spyware delivered via online ads ("AdFection"). Israeli firm Discover-Tech's ad infrastructure distributed Candiru spyware (now "Integrity Labs") that infected 45 Al Jazeera Windows devices in 2024–25; malicious ads seen across hundreds of sensitive networks incl. the Pentagon, IAEA, and ICC. (Devdiscourse/Reuters)
  • Ahold Delhaize: websites/apps offline for a 5th day. Dutch Justice Minister called on Ahold to file a criminal complaint; company says no customer/associate/partner data was taken; Albert Heijn doesn't expect online delivery back before Sunday. Physical stores open. (Reuters)
  • CISA federal patch deadline TODAY (Oct 16) for Ivanti Connect Secure CVE-2026-104935 (auth bypass → root RCE, actively exploited by UTA0576). (Security Magazine)
  • Proofpoint buying Varonis for $6.3B all-cash — major cyber industry M&A. (IT Security News)
  • Also on the radar: Silent Lynx exploiting a WinRAR flaw to deploy reverse shells in CIS government attacks; PEERSTITCH malware deployed via a FortiOS flaw to bypass checks on tagged VPN sessions. (Techmaniacs cyber briefing)

5. Court cases

  • Murdaugh retrial: "urgent matters" hearing TODAY at 10 AM ET in Lexington County. Judge McCaslin hears heated discovery fights — raw cellphone extraction files, DNA, FARO crime-scene scans, ballistics — ahead of the April 5, 2027 retrial. Follow-up hearing Nov 13. (Greenville News)
  • Birchmore/Farwell federal murder trial — day 5 today. Two FBI agents testifying (forensic expert Christopher Beckstrom, Special Agent Heidi Kelsch). Thursday: Sandra Birchmore's friend Lesley Davis told jurors she urged Canton police to investigate Farwell the day after Birchmore died; a state police investigator acknowledged no messages between the pair were found on Farwell's phone at first — federal investigators later recovered thousands. (Enterprise News, WJAR)
  • FTC v. Amazon Prime jury trial continues in Seattle; no fresh developments this morning. Netanyahu trial: no session (Mandelblit testimony resumes Oct 18–22).

The bottom line

  • Russian drones kill 3 across Ukraine overnight, cut power to ~370,000
  • Reuters: the White House directly ordered Ukraine's Starshield restrictions
  • Trump called Ukrainian refinery strikes "a disgrace" in a Newsmax interview
  • Trump: US "may have to" strike Iran's Pickaxe Mountain
  • Putin decreed local assets of French, German, Swedish, Dutch companies placed under temporary management
  • Russia claims 644 Ukrainian drones shot down overnight across 26 regions

Evening brief · Thursday, October 15, 2026

Evening news brief — Thu 2026-10-15, ~5 PM CT

Biggest story today: Houthis struck the Yemeni government's seat of power in Aden, and Zelensky publicly walked away from Trump's energy ceasefire. The IEA met today and agreed to speed up oil/diesel stock releases.

1. World escalation

Houthis hit Yemen's presidential palace complex in Aden — missiles struck near the Maashiq compound, seat of the internationally recognized government; PM and cabinet survived; health minister says 5 killed, 16 wounded. Reuters and AP carried separate accounts. First time the Houthis have gone after Aden's seat of government.

TLF live blog, Reuters, AP

Saudi coalition says it intercepted a cruise missile in the Medina region; Houthis deny any attacks today — coalition spox Turki al-Maliki announced the interception; Houthi spox Saree called the Medina claim a lie. Neither the missile's origin nor attribution is established — developing.

TLF live blog, Al Jazeera

NYT investigation: Saudi air defenses are struggling — radar blind spots facing Yemen, expensive interceptors burning against cheap drones, rigid command structures; Riyadh has leaned on its Turkey–Pakistan defense pact for intel/comms support, no combat deployment.

NYT via TLF

US Embassy in Saudi now requires special approval for government staff to use Saudi airports — travel-security step as KKIA closure is expected to extend and airlines keep avoiding the kingdom.

TLF live blog

UK defense secretary to ask Hegseth about the Starshield outage — UK trying to "bridge" the US and Ukraine back together after Zelensky publicly accused Washington of restricting his access to the military satellite network.

Washington Examiner

IEA board agreed today to speed up emergency oil and diesel stock releases — 32 nations agreed to release remaining ~100M bbl of oil and 20M+ bbl of diesel ASAP; figure came in below the 50M diesel barrels France had floated. Trump pressed EU countries to draw down or face a possible US diesel export ban ahead of Nov 3 midterms.

Reuters

Investigation: Houthis attempting to build more advanced missiles with Chinese-sourced components — operational deployment unconfirmed. Worth watching given the Aden reach.

TLF live blog

Poland: no fresh developments Thursday — court was to rule Wednesday on custody of Krzysztof N., 66, charged with plotting to overthrow the state with stockpiled explosives; no outcome in English coverage yet.

Nvidia DGX Spark 64GB arrives Oct 23, starting at $4,999 — price reveal for the desktop-tier RTX Spark AI PC ahead of Friday's laptop launch events.

Technobezz

Nvidia RTX Spark launch events open tomorrow (Fri Oct 16) globally — hands-on demos for gaming, creative work, local AI; laptop preorders since Oct 7, Surface Laptop Ultra among launch systems; compact desktops in November.

Technobezz

Nothing major new from Apple or Google today.

3. Open source

Libreboot 26.10 "Ominous Olive" released today — full UEFI support via the MrChromebox EDK2 payload (now the default), making Windows compatible on libreboot machines for the first time; GRUB/SeaBIOS kept as EFI builds.

libreboot.org via alobbs

dev.to

Pacific/BleepingComputer, reconbee

tech-insider.org

Morning brief · Thursday, October 15, 2026

Morning brief — Thu 2026-10-15, ~9 AM CT

Sweep window: last ~11 hours (since the 10 PM CT brief). Overnight's big moves: Zelensky formally ended the energy-ceasefire pause and Ukraine hit the Ryazan refinery within hours; two more ships sank near Hormuz; CISA added Palo Alto PAN-OS and Ahsay flaws to KEV; Nvidia's RTX Spark launch is tomorrow with Nemotron 3.5 Bolt 74B fully open source; India's Supreme Court struck down Yes Bank's $884M AT1 write-off.

1. World escalation

  • Zelensky declared the energy-ceasefire pause OVER — "The block is out. We're done." In an FT interview, he said Ukraine held fire on Russian refineries for three days to comply with Washington's wishes while Russia kept hitting Ukrainian cities; condition for renewed restraint: more Patriot interceptors from the US. He accused the US of withholding ballistic-missile early warnings and called the Starlink restriction "the will, not a technical problem."

Source: CNN

  • Ukraine struck the Ryazan oil refinery overnight — first refinery hit since Trump's Oct 11 announcement. Rosneft-owned plant (~5% of Russian refining capacity), fire reported; Russia's MoD claimed 4 Flamingo cruise missiles + 69 drones used. Kremlin's Peskov accused Kyiv of contradicting US peace efforts; Moscow said it hit 7 Ukrainian energy facilities Wednesday.

Source: WAMC/NPR, Reuters

  • Russia overnight Oct 14–15: Zelensky claims 850+ drones launched at 15 Ukrainian regions; also hit Borisoglebsk airfield, damaging 6 Russian Su-34M bombers. Aggregators report 13 killed Oct 6–15 across Kyiv, Kharkiv, Lutsk, Rivne.

Source: Political.org

  • Saudi coalition downed a drone over the Eastern Province early Thursday; also says it intercepted a cruise missile over Medina — Houthis deny the Medina claim outright. Saree called the Saudi account a "shameless and brazen lie," saying no operations were carried out Thursday; the coalition notably did not assign blame. Riyadh airport remains suspended; dozens of Jeddah flights canceled/delayed. EU–Gulf summit slated for Oct 24 in Saudi Arabia was postponed over security concerns.

Source: Unbiased Headlines, TBS News

  • TWO more ships SANK near Hormuz Wednesday: Singapore-flagged GFS Pride (container) + Antigua-flagged Cape Dao (bulk) — 2nd and 3rd commercial sinkings since Feb 28 per IMO. GFS Pride was hit Oct 13, all 21 crew evacuated; Cape Dao was struck Sept 23 (one crewman killed) and finally went down after failed salvage. Iran's IRGC claimed a container ship hit a mine on an "unauthorized" route — unverified. UKMTO: 15 attacks Oct 6–14.

Source: Reuters, Crisis.zone analysis

  • Poland: still no English-language outcome on Krzysztof N.'s Wednesday custody ruling. Carrying forward from yesterday — rechecking.

Source: Reuters

2. Tech products

  • Nvidia RTX Spark laptops go on sale TOMORROW (Oct 16); Nemotron 3.5 Bolt 74B releases today. 74B-parameter MoE with 9B active per token, 2-bit quantization-aware training, fits in 24GB; fully open source including training data, weights, and recipes (llama.cpp, vLLM, Ollama, LM Studio at launch). PAIR (open-source AI workload router) is GA; Broadcast 2.3 ships with an MCP server.

Source: Tech Times

3. Open source

  • CISA added four flaws to KEV: Palo Alto PAN-OS CVE-2026-0322 (management-interface RCE, CVSS 8.6, "very limited" exploitation so far), Cisco SEG CVE-2026-76519, and Ahsay CVE-2026-105133/CVE-2026-105134. Federal agencies have until Oct 17. Palo Alto: no special config needed to exploit; restrict management access to trusted IPs. Public PoC for CVE-2026-0322 already observed.

Source: Help Net Security

5. Major court cases

  • India's Supreme Court ruled Yes Bank's $884M AT1 bond write-off illegal. Upheld the Bombay HC's quashing of the March 2020 write-down of ₹8,415 crore in Additional Tier-1 bonds during the bank's rescue; Yes Bank, RBI, and the central government's appeals dismissed. Yes Bank shares plunged ~12.5% and hit the lower circuit.

Source: Reuters

*Watch for the 5 PM brief: Kyiv/Ryazan escalation fallout, Hormuz shipping (any new sinkings), and the RTX Spark launch day tomorrow.*

The bottom line

  • Zelensky declared the energy-ceasefire pause OVER — "The block is out. We're done."
  • Ukraine struck the Ryazan oil refinery overnight — first refinery hit since Trump's Oct 11 announcement
  • Russia overnight Oct 14–15: Zelensky claims 850+ drones launched at 15 Ukrainian regions; also hit Borisoglebsk airfield, damaging 6 Russian Su-34M bombers

  • Reuters analysis: Saturday's airport strike was the kingdom's deadliest attack in a decade (13 killed, 300+ wounded); notes MBS's Vision 2030 bet of transforming the economy while staying out of regional wars is now directly tested. Also: UKMTO data showed 24 ships hit in the two weeks to Oct 11 — the most intense shipping-attack period since early March. Reuters / Barron's
  • Zelensky went public on Starlink — accused SpaceX of hampering Ukrainian drones for attack and defense as US–Kyiv ties fray; Eutelsat shares jumped Wednesday on bets Europe's satellite providers benefit from the strain. TBS News

Developing — treating as rumor. investinglive
  • Poland: no fresh developments; Wednesday's court custody ruling for Krzysztof N. (66, charged with plotting the Tusk/Kosiniak-Kamysz attack) hadn't appeared in English coverage by 10 PM CT. Reuters

  • Apple closed above $5 trillion market cap for the first time ever — $5.005T at a $342.96 record close, making Apple the second company to finish a session above $5T after Nvidia; the WSJ frames it as the capstone of the Tim Cook era (new CEO John Ternus started Sept 1). WSJ / 9to5Mac
  • xAI launched Grok Voice 3.0 today — the grok-voice-latest alias now auto-points to the new speech-to-speech model, so existing voice agents switched over with no deploy; it tops the Artificial Analysis speech-to-speech index at 86.9, ahead of OpenAI's GPT-Live-1 at 83.2. dev.to

3. Open source

  • Petal (petal.live) — ex-CoScreen team shipped a free, open-source pair-programming and screen-sharing tool after Datadog sunset CoScreen in July; multi-user movable windows with labeled cursors, clickable typing/scrolling, persistent rooms, macOS/Windows/web via LiveKit, hosted or self-hosted. alobbs digest
  • Neckbeard — new DevOps/platform/SRE plugin for coding agents: analyzes the repo and emits reviewable cloud infrastructure + monthly cost estimates across AWS/GCP/Azure using tested OpenTofu modules, with GitHub Actions/GitLab CI and serverless-or-K8s support; installs into Claude Code and other SKILL.md-speaking agents. alobbs digest / github.com

4. Cybersecurity

  • Cisco SEG zero-day (CVE-2026-76519) landed on CISA KEV Wednesday — federal agencies ordered patched by Saturday; Cisco says a "limited number of customers" are affected; no disclosure yet of how many appliances were compromised or what attackers did post-exploit. The Register
  • Ivanti backstory, via Dark Reading — Ivanti actually found part of CVE-2026-104935 in July through its LLM-based vuln-hunting project and patched 25.1.3.0, but was still backporting the fix to older supported versions when UTA0576's exploit chain hit; CISA orders federal agencies patched by Friday. Dark Reading / BleepingComputer
  • GitHub shipped an AI Scan security dashboard (Oct 13) — org-level metrics: findings generated/resolved, remediation rate, autofix acceptance rates, per-repo and trend views; public preview for GHAS customers on github.com. pondero.ai
  • Fresh ransomware-leak claims tonight (unverified tracker reports): Akira claims 84 GB from Torns Enterprises including employee passports/visas; N0N claims it breached Interior Technologies, a US smart-building/surveillance integrator, and disabled client-site surveillance feeds pending settlement. Claims only — no company confirmations. qpulse / redpacketsecurity

5. Major court cases

  • Tyreek Hill civil trial: mixed verdict Tuesday — Miami jury found Hill liable on 2 battery counts (Jan 2024, April 2025) against estranged wife Lakeeta Vaccaro, awarded $500k compensatory, no punitive damages; cleared him on 8 other claims. (AP via WVLT, Reuters)
  • OpenAI engineer charged with bugging exec meetings — DOJ arrested Saudi national Abdulrahman Alfozan, 35, on Oct 9; says he planted a Seeed XIAO ESP32-S3 recording device (encrypted, concealed in toilet paper) in a USB port behind an exec-room TV around Sept 28; faces up to 5 years. OpenAI says it used its own AI models to ID him; no evidence of model weights, source code, or customer data exfiltration. USA Today / Reuters via LA Post / The Register
  • Apple moved Tuesday to overturn the $5.7B Taction patent verdict — largest patent verdict in US history (jury found Sept 25 that Apple's Taptic Engine infringed haptic patents); Apple calls the award "untethered to any evidence," and noted the judge himself said he wasn't sure the verdict form reflected what the jury meant. Reuters
  • Qualcomm v. Arm: mixed Delaware verdict Tuesday — jury awarded $2 in nominal damages; found Arm breached obligations to supply patches/tools and interfered with Qualcomm's Meta relationship, but also sided with Arm on several claims; post-verdict issues (including a 5-year royalty-suspension clause) left for Judge Noreika. Catch-up from Oct 13, not previously reported. neoteo
  • Marilyn Mosby: mortgage-fraud charge dismissed with prejudice — federal prosecutors declined to retry after the 4th Circuit overturned the conviction; her two perjury convictions stand after SCOTUS declined her appeal. focalnews

The bottom line

  • Houthis claim "large-scale" missile/drone attack on Saudi targets Wednesday
  • Saudi hit Houthi fuel infrastructure Tuesday
  • Reuters analysis: Saturday's airport strike was the kingdom's deadliest attack in a decade
  • Zelensky went public on Starlink

Source: OilPrice, Defence-Blog

  • Starlink/StarShield restrictions on Ukrainian forces CONFIRMED. Presidential adviser Serhii Beskrestnov: SpaceX introduced speed restrictions (~160 km/h) on military Starshield terminals overnight with no warning, disrupting drone missions; the 7th Air Assault Corps confirmed 10–20 second dropouts at 110–120 km/h forcing mission cancellations. Fedorov later announced partial restoration up to 160 km/h. Polish FM Sikorski publicly rebuked Musk on X; Trump suggested Ukraine needs a "new leader," which Musk echoed.

Source: Aeronaut Media, Adria Defense

  • WSJ: Aramco Dhahran HQ damage is extensive — fire spread across several floors, parts of the roof collapsed. The building hit houses the CEO's office plus oil-supply planning and scheduling; top three floors severely damaged, windows and doors blown out. Saudi Energy Ministry called it a "limited fire"; employees told to work from home, some functions shifted to global offices. Houthis vowed more attacks on Saudi airports and oil facilities; coalition says it intercepted a missile toward Riyadh Wednesday morning.

Source: WSJ, Reuters

  • Hormuz tanker war grinding on: Iran expanding strikes beyond the strait into the Gulf of Oman to keep oil prices elevated before the US midterms. Two senior Iranian officials told Reuters Tehran is using small-boat observers to pick targets after its radar was damaged; 5 incidents in 48 hours. Kpler: 20.8M barrels transited Oct 8 → 2.9M on Oct 11 (pre-war avg 17.1M); Brent above $106.

Source: Reuters

  • Axios: Netanyahu pressed Trump for renewed Iran strikes on a call last week (4 sources); White House denied it. Netanyahu raised Israeli intel that Iran is rebuilding its nuclear program (including Pickaxe Mountain enrichment concerns); Trump reportedly told him "go ahead and get ready" but made no commitment. Trump has publicly said no strikes before the Nov 3 midterms. IDF chief Zamir reportedly warned renewed fighting within 3 weeks could postpone Israel's Oct 27 election.

Source: Fact.net.in (Axios reporting), Unbiased Headlines

  • Two US carrier strike groups now in the Arabian Sea — USS George H.W. Bush joined USS George Washington (USNI fleet tracker, Oct 13); a third (USS Theodore Roosevelt) is en route. Restores a two-carrier presence for the first time since April; Pentagon adding 9,000–10,000 troops to the region by end of November.

Source: Army Recognition

  • Poland: Krzysztof N., 66, charged with 9 offenses over the Tusk assassination plot — court rules on custody today. Prosecutors: stockpiled a dozen "firecrackers with metal balls" as shrapnel, recruited a several-hundred-person online group; he pleaded not guilty citing physical and mental health issues of his age. No evidence of foreign-intel involvement.

Source: Reuters

2. Tech products

  • Meta extended Private Processing (confidential computing) to its AI glasses. Cloud-based confidential VMs backed by hardware TEEs now handle persistent user context (streaming transcription, contextual search, long-term recall) with data encrypted and inaccessible to Meta itself; remote attestation before any personal context is transmitted.

Source: LavX News

  • ASML posted record Q3: €11.7B sales, €5.0B net income — and warned 2027–2028 chip-tool output won't fully meet AI demand. Sold 113 new lithography systems; guided Q4 €14.2–15.2B and full-year €44–45B. Some customers are already asking about 2029–2030 orders.

Source: GlobeNewswire (official release)

  • Japan to invest up to $21B in two GlobalFoundries chip fabs in New York. Jointly owned by US and Japanese interests, GF operates; part of the $550B US-Japan investment deal. US government stake in GF rises to ~7%; first fab online 2029; initial customers include Apple and Renesas.

Source: Reuters

3. Open source

  • ASF promoted three projects to Top-Level status: Apache Auron (native vectorized query accelerator, 2x faster than Spark 3.5), Apache Reqsign (Rust HTTP request signer for cloud services, no heavy SDKs), and Apache ResilientDB (Byzantine fault-tolerant database).

Source: Apache Software Foundation

  • KDE Plasma 6.8 released today — timed to KDE's 30th birthday. Fixes NVIDIA window-arranging lag, unreliable Flatpak auto-updates in Discover, KRunner keyboard navigation, Slow Keys key-repeat; Spectacle screen recording improvements; second half of the "Union" theming tech preview.

Source: NewInLinux

  • Liquid AI released LFM2.5-24B-A2B — open-weight 24B-parameter MoE reasoning model (2B active per token) built for on-device AI agents. 131K context, GGUF/MLX/ONNX builds, day-one llama.cpp/vLLM/SGLang support; vendor benchmarks claim strong agentic results vs larger rivals.

Source: Unite.AI

4. Cybersecurity

  • Cisco confirmed an actively exploited Secure Email Gateway zero-day: CVE-2026-76519 (CVSS 9.8) — crafted email attachment → root command execution, no authentication needed. Path traversal in the AMP file-scanning feature; affects gateways with File Reputation enabled and Content Scanner Tools older than 25.3.0.5525. CISA added it to KEV the same day. Cisco says rebuild (don't just upgrade) virtual appliances showing compromise.

Source: BleepingComputer, The Register

  • Ivanti CVE-2026-104935 exploitation confirmed at scale: Previdian honeypots logged 105 exploit attempts from 50 IPs (Singapore/US); watchTowr expects mass exploitation. Volexity: attacker UTA0576 has chained the auth bypass with a still-unpatched privilege escalation for root RCE on fully patched appliances since Oct 3. CISA KEV deadline Oct 16.

Source: Carthage Electronics CVE threat brief

  • Anthropic warned small AI models may soon self-replicate across IoT devices. Experiments suggest models under 30B parameters are months away from autonomously finding vulnerable devices (smart ovens, off-brand Android TV boxes), copying themselves over, and spreading without human help — forming botnets with no central switch-off. GLM-5.2-class models could do end-to-end replication by year's end at current progress rates.

Source: Reuters

  • Ledger hardware tampering confirmed (follow-up to the Oct 12 CryptoBilis story). Unauthorized implants in reseller-sold wallets can expose recovery phrases and bypass authenticity checks — buy direct from Ledger only.

Source: CoinDesk

FTC opening: Amazon enrolled 35M+ people in Prime without consent and made cancellation a labyrinth ("Iliad flow," up to 7 clicks); Amazon says the FTC is litigating font choices and button sizes. Nine-person jury, ~4 weeks, potential billions in penalties and refunds.

Night brief — Tuesday Oct 13, 2026 (~10 PM CT)

Sweep window: last ~5 hours (since the 5 PM CT brief). Big night: the energy "ceasefire" is effectively dead on both sides, and the Houthis hit Aramco's headquarters in Dhahran.

1. World escalation

  • Russia hit Kyiv with ballistic missiles Tuesday evening, struck thermal power plant No. 4. Zelensky says Ukraine got no advance warning from Western partners — second night in a row — and that "the facts show that the Russians do not consider themselves bound to abide by what the president of the United States said." One person confirmed killed in a burning apartment building; Trump denied intelligence sharing had stopped. (Reuters, Guardian war briefing via Europe Says)
  • Single-source, unverified: Ukraine reportedly struck a Russian oil depot in Valuyki (Belgorod Oblast) overnight with 500+ drones — would be the first Ukrainian energy strike since Trump's ceasefire announcement; Kyiv reportedly answered "we will burn Russian refineries." US had warned it could cut intel sharing and freeze PURL if Kyiv resumed energy strikes. Developing, treat with caution. (BritBrief, BritBrief follow-up)
  • Houthi ballistic missile hit Saudi Aramco's headquarters complex in Dhahran on Tuesday night — an office tower, top three floors damaged, building set on fire (later put out). Saudi Energy Ministry confirmed the hit; no injuries. This is the first strike to reach Aramco's HQ campus — the administrative heart of the Saudi oil industry. (Reuters via Philippine Daily Post, Bloomberg via Mint)
  • Coalition said it intercepted three Houthi cruise missiles and two drones Tuesday over Riyadh and the south; four people injured in Riyadh by falling debris. (JFeed)
  • Trump on Truth Social: Houthis "behaving very badly," probably at Iran's direction to push oil prices before the Nov 3 midterms — said he thought they'd learned their lesson from last year's US bombing and warned "I will never forget." (Seoul Economic Daily, NY Post)
  • Houthis say Saudi-led coalition hit them in Yemen on Tuesday — airstrikes on Kamaran island (Red Sea), Qanawis district near Hodeida, and Jawf province; rebels also claim they shot down a Saudi drone over Saada. No Saudi comment yet. (AP via Reflector)

Evening brief · Tuesday, October 13, 2026

Evening news brief — Tue Oct 13, 2026 (~5 PM CT)

Two corrections to earlier briefs are at the top of sections 4 and 5 — they matter more than any single new headline today.

1. World escalation

  • Energy ceasefire: Russia says it hit no Ukrainian energy targets overnight — first clean night since Trump's Sunday announcement. Moscow's daily strike summary mentioned transport and logistics but no energy facilities. Zelensky says Ukraine has held off refinery strikes for two days and Russia failed to reciprocate; Kremlin spokesman Peskov would only say "contacts are ongoing." Trump acknowledged Monday there have been "violations on both sides."

Source: AnewZ (Reuters wire), NY Post

  • FT and CNN report the State Department and Pentagon warned Ukrainian and European officials that US assistance would stop if Kyiv doesn't rein in long-range strikes. This is the follow-up to the previously unverified PURL/intel-cutoff claim; the White House still hasn't commented. Developing.

Source: NY Post

  • Hormuz is now the worst tanker war in two weeks — 24 ships struck in that window, six on Sunday alone, the heaviest single day since the war began Feb. 28. Oil flows through the strait are under half pre-war levels. ISW warns Iran is getting better at targeting ships and may be improving its anti-ship missile capabilities.

Source: NY Post

  • IRGC claims it struck a supertanker in the Strait of Hormuz that had its transponder off (reported Oct 13, incident allegedly a day earlier). Unconfirmed — vessel identity and damage unknown. Single-source state-media-adjacent reporting; developing.

Source: Dainik Jagran roundup

  • WSJ: Iran is fortifying its nuclear sites and rallying the public for a possible return to fighting. Tehran has warned Arab officials it could strike regional targets including Saudi oil facilities; a third US carrier strike group and another Marine expeditionary unit are steaming toward the region; Trump has publicly mulled hitting Iran's Pickaxe Mountain nuclear site.

Source: WSJ

  • Trump warned the Houthis on Tuesday and said he "might" ask Turkey's Erdogan to help hit them. Comes after the weekend's airport attacks; the US has held off striking since the May 2025 ceasefire on US vessels.

Source: NY Post

  • Poland's first assassination-plot suspect is now identified as Krzysztof N., 66 — charged with nine offenses including plotting to forcibly overthrow state authorities using stockpiled explosives found in his apartment. Prosecutors say he built a group of several hundred followers via online recordings; he faces 2–15 years. A court rules Wednesday on keeping him in custody.

Source: Reuters

2. Tech products

  • Nvidia open-sourced Run:ai, its GPU orchestration platform, today — moving it from proprietary to open source inside the DSX AI Factory ecosystem. Also released Model Streamer (streams model weights into GPU memory, already upstream in vLLM and SGLang) and Grove (a Kubernetes API for agentic workloads). Single-source reporting.

Source: Blockchain News

  • Nvidia shipped its RTX Spark software ecosystem update today: Adobe is optimizing Photoshop and Premiere for RTX Spark (up to 2x faster AI workflows), NVIDIA Broadcast 2.3 adds an MCP server so local AI agents can drive the app, and Blender 5.3 (November) gets DLSS Ray Reconstruction. Single-source reporting.

Source: Blockchain News

  • Nothing new from Apple or Google this afternoon — the morning brief carried the full Welcome Home event and the Fitbit Edge launch. No new launches since.

3. Open source

  • GitHub Digest Oct 13: Supervisor-Skills (9.4k stars — turns research experience into usable Claude/agent skills), artex-global (Go autonomous pentest framework driven by LLM agents, 1.4k stars), RSI-Anything (recursive self-improvement via world models), founder-skill (11 free Claude skills for testing a business idea).

Source: AlexTech.ai

  • NodeSource Weekly (Oct 13): Node.js 26.11.1 patch release; N|Solid 6.3.8 now supports OpenVEX — so it can tell you whether a CVE actually affects your deployment instead of just flagging the dependency.

Source: NodeSource

4. Cybersecurity

  • CORRECTION — the morning brief called October Patch Tuesday "unusually quiet"; it was actually Microsoft's largest ever. ~1,413 CVEs per the MSRC, including three zero-days: CVE-2026-96951 (CVSS 8.8, ACTIVELY EXPLOITED Windows Shell Mark-of-the-Web bypass via command injection), CVE-2026-108398 (.NET Framework, found by Google Project Zero, no known exploitation), and CVE-2026-92707 (MessagePack-CSharp, publicly disclosed). Microsoft also debuted "risk cohorts" — provisional CVE groupings for shared assessment. Patch Windows first.

Source: DeafNews

  • Ivanti Connect Secure zero-day actively exploited: CVE-2026-104935 (CVSS 8.6), an authentication-bypass flaw allowing unauthenticated remote command execution. Ivanti's Oct 13 advisory says exploitation happened before disclosure as a true zero-day against a "limited number of customers"; CISA added it to KEV the same day. Worse: the attacker chained it with a second, still-unpatched privilege escalation flaw. Volexity published a full analysis — if you run ICS, patch now and don't trust the Integrity Checker alone.

Source: IT Security News, Cybersecurity News, SecurityOnline

  • Sharecare: ~318k email addresses surfaced on Have I Been Pwned, tied to ShinyHunters' August extortion campaign. 73% were already in HIBP from earlier breaches, so the exposure is mostly recycled — but it's another reminder that ShinyHunters kept what they stole.

Source: Undercode News

  • France supermarket fridge-hack: investigators are hunting the attackers; still no claim of responsibility. French security firm Onyphe says outdated, vulnerable Danfoss refrigeration controllers remain widely exposed online; some impacted stores are back up.

Source: DevDiscourse (syndicated), CNN

  • Ahold Delhaize's Tuesday update: a controlled restart of systems is underway, Albert Heijn deliveries are resuming, but some stores still have fresh-food shortages. The company says there's no evidence of customer or employee data theft; the Dutch NCSC says it sees no link to the French supermarket attack.

Source: LinksGraph, Reuters via KELO-FM, SecurityWeek

5. Major court cases

  • CORRECTION — the FTC v. Amazon antitrust trial did NOT start today. The October 13, 2026 trial date was superseded: Judge John Chun denied Amazon's bid on Oct 9 to push the trial from March to June 2027, and the trial is set for March 29, 2027. The settled September 2025 Prime case was a separate consumer-protection trial — that's what recent "trial opens" coverage was about, not the monopoly case. Apologies for the mix-up in yesterday's and this morning's notes.

Source: MLex, PYMNTS

  • Netanyahu trial: no session today. Mandelblit's defense-witness testimony resumes Oct 18–22. Nothing new.
  • Murdaugh retrial: no fresh developments. Oct 16 in-person hearing on evidentiary disputes is the next milestone.

The bottom line

  • Energy ceasefire: Russia says it hit no Ukrainian energy targets overnight — first clean night since Trump's Sunday announcement
  • FT and CNN report the State Department and Pentagon warned Ukrainian and European officials that US assistance would stop if Kyiv doesn't rein in long-range strikes
  • Hormuz is now the worst tanker war in two weeks — 24 ships struck in that window, six on Sunday alone, the heaviest single day since the war began Feb. 28

  • WSJ: Iran is fortifying its nuclear sites and rallying the public for a possible return to fighting
  • Trump warned the Houthis on Tuesday and said he "might" ask Turkey's Erdogan to help hit them

Trump doubles down on energy-ceasefire claim, blames Zelensky for continued fighting.

https://www.europesays.com/russia/75503/
